oracle_clues: The expected result is stated as 'np.inf result as produced by numpy.hypot' (oracle).
The incorrect result is stated as '= np.nan' for hypot(np.inf, np.nan) (observed behavior).

category_specific_evidence: Special values involved: NaN/inf pairings in hypot; the fix is described as “Fixed hypot bug wherein hypot(np.inf, np.nan)=np.nan instead of the expected np.inf result as produced by numpy.hypot.”

Special-value pathway motivation: “Unfortunately `maximum(np.nan, np.inf) = np.nan` so those cases will lead to incorrect output.” This indicates hypot’s use of maximum/minimum must account for NaN/inf interactions.
+infinity detection is explicitly handled via `idx_inf = lax.bitwise_or(isposinf(x1), isposinf(x2))` after `x1, x2 = lax.abs(x1), lax.abs(x2)`, showing special-case logic for +inf.

Signed/zero handling is explicitly branched on equality to zero: `x = _where(x1 == 0, x1, x1 * lax.sqrt(1 + lax.square(lax.div(x2, _where(x1 == 0, lax._ones(x1), x1)))))`, replacing earlier `lax.select(x1 == 0, ...)` logic.

Complex-valued inputs are special-cased: hypot checks `if dtypes.issubdtype(x1.dtype, np.complexfloating):` and raises a `DeprecationWarning` today (“Passing complex-valued inputs to hypot is deprecated…”)—separate from NaN/inf but still indicates special handling for non-real values.
reproduction_risks: To reproduce the reported bug, include the NaN/inf pairing specifically where one argument is +infinity and the other is NaN (`hypot(np.inf, np.nan)`), because the incorrect behavior is stated for that exact pairing.

The internal failure mode is tied to operations involving `maximum`/`minimum` with NaNs; the evidence explicitly notes `maximum(np.nan, np.inf) = np.nan`, so reproduction should reach that computation path (i.e., not short-circuit before max/min).

Because the implementation has an explicit zero branch (`_where(x1 == 0, ...)`), ensure your test includes coverage of cases where one argument becomes exactly 0 after abs, if you’re comparing against the corrected logic.

Complex-valued inputs to `jax.numpy.hypot` are deprecated and will emit a `DeprecationWarning` (per tests and implementation), so reproduction that accidentally uses complex dtype may introduce warning/behavior differences unrelated to NaN/inf.
